headline: Inventing the Renaissance takes December.
deck: A clean win at the top for once — and the tie moved down to second, where an even 4–4 head-to-head forced the fall-through to first-place votes.
intro: All — eight of you ranked nine candidates this round. Inventing the Renaissance (Palmer) took it on 54 points, six clear of the field, and reads December. No tiebreaker was needed for the win; the drama was one row lower.
outcome: Winner: Inventing the Renaissance (54)   ·   Runner-up: Say Nothing (48, on first-place votes)   ·   Relegated: none — nine candidates, no relegation line
discussionLead: I think I might be gluten intolerant after all of the recent focus on grain. Fun discussion last night, with a few takeaways — the retrospectively bizarre one being the progression of Genghis Khan → Sapiens → Against the Grain. Not planned, but an interesting run of related topics.
tieIntro: Say Nothing and Something Rich and Strange both finished on 48 points. The methodology calls for a Condorcet head-to-head first: ignore the rest of the ballot and ask how each voter ranked these two against one another.
tieVerdict: The head-to-head split 4–4 — dead even, no winner, nothing to separate them. That sends the tie through to the next breaker, first-place votes, where Say Nothing leads 2–1 and takes second. Both books stay on the candidate list at full strength.
notes: The second even-split fall-through. August 2026 was the first: a pair that matched on Borda and then matched again head-to-head. A 4–4 split with eight voters is the cleanest possible way for Condorcet to say nothing at all.

Eight ballots, five different first choices. Inventing the Renaissance, Say Nothing and An Immense World took two firsts each; Something Rich and Strange and Born to Run took one apiece. Nobody ran away with the top of the ballot — the winner won on depth, not on firsts.

An Immense World is the polarizing one. It tied for the most first-place votes in the field with two, and still finished fourth on 43 points. Enough voters left it low to cost it eleven points on the leader.
Say Nothing is runner-up again — second month running, second tie running. In November it was level at the top and lost the head-to-head; this time it was level at second and won the fall-through.
No debuts. Every book on this ballot had been polled before. The field is down to nine after November's three relegations and Endurance's selection, which is why nothing was relegated this round.
The River of Doubt reaches twenty-two polls and finished last on 27 points, with no first-place votes.
